title: Creating, reading, changing and deleting files from the command line

videos.script: On the server there is no file manager. When a backup log needs reading, a folder of old invoices needs moving, or a hundred temporary files need deleting, Ana does it by typing. {{server}} Four things are done to files, on any system: create them, read them, change them, and delete them. A file manager does each with a click. The command line does each with a short word, and does it to one file or to a thousand with the same effort. {{four}} That second part is the power and the danger. A command that deletes every temporary file deletes them all at once, with no Recycle Bin behind it. So this lesson is also about the habits that let you type those commands calmly: looking before deleting, and knowing which characters overwrite. {{habits}} In this lesson you will create folders and files, and read a long log without opening all of it. You will add to a file and overwrite one. You will copy, move and rename, pick many files at once with wildcards, and delete safely. Then the same in PowerShell, which can tell you what it would do before it does it. {{steps}} The transcripts come from lesson 3's server, in bash and in PowerShell 7 on the same machine. The Command Prompt equivalents are listed, not run. {{honest}}
